history:

Persona rounds 4-7: round 5 N1 "an agent can start the code's surfaces itself"; round 7 listed R1-R7, "R7: the terminal-confirmation opt-in is passable by design", seven risks "that only sandboxing removes". The stakeholder decided OQ-29 on 3 Oct (commit 23fcbd1, proposal.md:75 D5): "no software surface proves who acted, so ParleyInn rests owner acts on the sandbox ... and does not try to defeat an unsandboxed one". Per-act WebAuthn became optional hardening. The sandbox work is parked in plan 2610031222, still status 🔲. The SRS carries it: T21 (06-security.md:62), R3/R7 (:81, :85), OWN-22 (05c:38, "An unsandboxed agent can forge the risk acceptance itself"), M1 plan (12-delivery-plan.md:35-37, widening acts "only through the CLI at a terminal"). Scope limit: the threat-source row says a same-user process is in scope "For principal acts only" (06-security.md:33).

THE 32 ROUNDS. Round 1 M1 (blind.md:15) split owner acts into room acts and principal acts; v2 D11 (domain-model-v2.md:86-91): room acts "signed by a seat key", principal acts "signed by a device key at an authenticated surface". Before the split, comment, join, leave, kick, bar, present and pick sat in the Owner act list (4d5c43d^:docs/domain-model.md:129-137), and OWN-12 made every CLI verb that writes an owner act "refuse unless its standard input and output are a terminal" (5ee17ad^). After it, OWN-12's last sentence gives room-act verbs "no OWN-11 class" and no terminal test. Round 6 Q8 (blind-6.md:22): the facilitator acts "through its node's CLI ... signed with its device seat". Round 10 Q2 (f7a0e80): "an act a seat key signs is a room act wherever it is taken". Round 12 Q8 and Q10 (243928c): "the CLI or TUI at a terminal"; a device seat posts and links from the CLI. Round 29 Q10 (9627c0b): a "read-only CLI verb ... whose output is not a terminal" is recall. Round 30 Q12: `parinn configuration accept` "at a terminal with nothing more asked". The only model sentence on agent-originated calls (index.md:121-122, "a skill's call is the agent's own tool call") settled a slash-command conflict (S12, blind.md:69; v2 D19) and covers skills only. Round 5 only reworded "act" to "tool call". Round 20 listed "unsandboxed agent" under optional, not chased (blind-20.md:50). The rounds never reached zero: 8-24 needs-fix each, ending at 8 in round 32, which the stakeholder stopped (blind-32.md:44). Recommended options were taken without asking (blind-5.md:13).

REPAIR PHASE, 8 Oct. v1 R1/R2 (a run's tool call is never a principal surface; device seats act only at a principal surface), v2 F1, v4 R2, v5 S4. The v5-core review still had five principal-surface or install needs-fix (tmux, screen, cron, keys into an open TUI: v5-core.findings.json #0, #1, #6, #7, #8). v6 opened "added text drew new findings" and ruled T1 (repair-v6-rulings.md:19): "Say this once, in Principal surface", quote the SRS residual risks R1, R3 and R7, "Do not invent authentication". The four v6 probes had no principal-surface finding. Commit 03298ac (8 Oct 13:36): the stakeholder ruled the search "never changes its text", so v1-v6 stay in annotated-v*/ and docs/domain-model never received them.

CURRENT TEXT. Reported needs-fix in 6 of 7 strong v0 reviews (v0-all-r2 #12, #13; r3-partial #0; ga1-5-strong #0; ga2-4-strong #14; add-brv #1, #10; nopk-partial #11). explanation: The same-user-agent risk was raised and settled before the model existed (persona rounds 4-7, OQ-29): accepted as residual risks R1-R7 and parked in an unstarted sandbox plan, with the SRS saying so, but none of the entries the 32 rounds edited carries that. The rounds used a consistency-and-drift lens (.claude/agents/domain-model.md), so they classified "at a terminal" and "wherever it is taken" without asking who could satisfy them. history:
SRS. c72e02b already had T5 ("Malicious `.parinn.toml` enables per-prompt injection or trusts more provenance" / "Repository configuration may only tighten (SEC-11)"), SEC-11 and the §9.6 table of what repository configuration may set. After persona R7-2, the 2.0-draft SRS (966c80d, 3 Oct) added to ADM-04 that a change that "adds or ends a pin ... MUST take effect only after a widening act ... records its digest". Round 20 (ddc9fbf) had "a repository key making one MUST be ignored, audited and counted", now at 05a:17.

MODEL ROUNDS, vocabulary only. Round 1 M8 (configuration pins have no author); round 4 (blind-4.md:90, undefined "configuration pin and its author", defined in 359cbad as "A pin the principal's configuration declares, authored by its device seat on that node (PIN-01)"); round 6 Q7 (accept configuration "record its digest" is widening); round 9 Q9 (d407e08, blind-9.md:23, "a repository's `.parinn.toml`, which may only tighten the principal's configuration (ADM-04)", decided as a naming question); round 13 ("repository file" becomes repository configuration); round 14 Q7 ("repository configuration only tightens"); round 19 Q1 (three settings layers); round 21 Q5 (repository configuration cannot shorten retention); round 22 Q12 (blind-22.md:30, "tightening a rule level" is cut); round 23 Q5; round 28 Q8; round 30 Q12 (acceptance of the room-view component and launcher). No round asked what "tighten" means or whether a configuration pin waits for acceptance.

CURRENT TEXT. Acceptance is carried only for a retention policy (record.md:134-137), turning on the room-view component or launcher (components-and-surfaces.md:98-103) and as the listed widening act "accept configuration (recording its digest)" (acts-and-roles.md:78-79). Configuration pin (pins-and-context.md:41-42) cites PIN-01, and Record (record.md:11-13) cites ADM-04 for "tighten" although the direction rules live in SEC-11 and §9.6. Open conflict never raised: §9.6 lets an untrusted repository lower the pin budget or switch a restore path off, while the model says "Any principal act that removes a pin from a restore block ... is widening" (acts-and-roles.md:87-89). I3 itself allows omission by budget, "named by id and count".

REPAIR PHASE. v1 R5 (repository configuration "declares no pins and may make only changes a cut act could make"), v3 K7, v4 R4/R5. The v4-core review found the contradiction the repair added (#1, a cut act versus removing a pin from a restore block). v5 S2 ruled "turning off a restore path or lowering the pin budget is widening ... repository configuration never makes such a change". v5-core and v5-all had no F needs-fix. S2 contradicts SRS §9.6, so it would also need that table changed. Discarded by 03298ac. v0: needs-fix in 3 of 7 strong reviews (v0-all-r2 #15, ga1-5-strong #13, ga2-4-strong #16).
explanation: The configuration-pin half was raised by the persona security review and settled in the SRS (ADM-04 since 966c80d: acceptance with a recorded digest, repository keys ignored, audited and counted), but the 32 model rounds only touched the vocabulary (naming repository configuration, settings layers, retention) and never copied the rule into the Configuration pin entry. The model cites ADM-04 for "tighten" while the per-key meaning is in SEC-11 and §9.6, and the v0 reviewers, who by brief cannot read the SRS, see an undefined word and an untethered pin. The one real design conflict, §9.6 letting a repository lower the pin budget or turn restore off against the model's widening rule and I3, was never raised, and the v5 repair that forbade it contradicts the SRS table.

The rounds' reviewers worked from the domain-model agent's brief (terms, relations, model-versus-SRS drift; .claude/agents/domain-model.md:30-48) and were partitioned from R22 so Principal (principals-and-agents) and Bar/Admission (acts-and-roles) sat with different reviewers. The fix text exists only in research/ and was never applied.

R5 Q10 (blind-5.md:28): 'Managed policy lists certified service-account principal keys in its root-owned configuration, no signature; a principal key that a person, a service account or managed policy certified is a service account's; an uncertified one counts as a person's, which no check can prove.' R6 Q14: PRV-10 states certification. R10/R11 Q5 (blind-11.md:19): a principal key may certify a service account's key; chains never pass through another principal key. R14 Q6 (blind-14.md:21): a revoked service account stays one. R22 Q10 and R24 Q3 (blind-24.md:17, commit 7763836): 'revocable only by its certifier'. R26 Q9 and R28 Q2 (blind-28.md:16): the certificate or listing carries a 'relaying' mark; an unmarked listing counts as relaying, so trust grants naming it are refused. R30 Q10 (blind-30.md:25): the mark leaves the seat certificate; 'the service-account certificate or managed-policy listing in the key set decides it'. The model text never put the listing in the key set: Key set is 'the keys, certificates and revocations it holds' (seats-and-keys.md:75-76) and managed policy is a settings layer beside the record (record.md:8-14), while I10 allows only writer logs plus the key set (invariants.md:93-97). R4 had already amended Record to include the node's own key set for I10, so I10 was checked for keys but never for listings. Cumulatively these decisions mean a stranger's certificate, once in a node's key set, turns a person into a service account (no verdicts, OWN-27; trust grants naming it refused) and only the stranger can revoke it. The GA repair phase wrote the I10 half in a research copy ('each listing and each removal is recorded as a structural event that enters the node's key set (I10)', annotated-v6/principals-and-agents.md.ann:31-36); no repair ever wrote a countersign or consent rule; 03298ac reverted to the original text.

The consent half was never raised before the GA/SA security lens. R30 Q10's wording suggests the listing is in the key set, but no model text says so, so that decision is only half written.
